title: Interface contracts for components and pagination

blocks.text: Define meaning, cancellation, and ownership before framework hooks. The list accepts a page loader and item renderer; the loader exposes opaque pagination without leaking transport details. Parents cannot set internal loading flags, and the list cannot invent server cursors.

blocks.title: Request and response
blocks.text: PageLoader receives one structured request containing the stable query key, normalized filters, sort order, page limit, opaque cursor, and AbortSignal. It returns ordered items, nextCursor, and optionally an ordering version. No nextCursor means the end. The client stores and returns the opaque cursor without parsing or incrementing it.

blocks.title: Request guarantees
items: Use an explicit limit and normalized filter object so cache keys are deterministic.
Pass AbortSignal through every transport and transformation layer that can stop work.
On Retry, send the committed cursor again instead of deriving a later cursor.

blocks.title: Response guarantees
items: Every item has a stable ID, and continuation uses deterministic ordering.
nextCursor commits with its items and may be absent on the final page.
A repeated cursor becomes a contract error instead of an automatic loop.

blocks.text: InfiniteScrollList receives feedKey, initialPage, pageLoader, renderItem, getItemId, estimatedItemHeight, overscan, and restoration data. Optional callbacks report an error, committed page, or end. Do not expose observer instances, measurement nodes, raw scroll events, cursor setters, or contradictory state flags.

blocks.title: Viewport responsibilities
items: Render semantic containers, one sentinel, loading, inline Retry, and end states.
Expose aria-busy and concise announcements from controller state.
Capture anchor and focus identity before navigation.

blocks.title: Renderer responsibilities
items: Render one semantic item without loading pages.
Reserve media dimensions and report geometry changes.
Use stable item ID for rendering and measurement, never array index.

steps.title: 1. Initialize
steps.text: Normalize initialPage under feedKey and render it, or issue one initial request.

steps.title: 2. Request more
steps.text: Observer visibility and Load More invoke the same guarded loadNext command.

steps.title: 3. Cancel or replace
steps.text: Unmount or a new feedKey aborts work; generation checks reject late completion.

steps.title: 4. Recover
steps.text: Prior rows remain interactive, and Retry repeats failedCursor.

steps.title: 5. Finish
steps.text: No nextCursor disables loading and emits the end event once per generation.

blocks.text: Match IntersectionObserver root to the scroll container and tune rootMargin against page size and latency. Recreate it only when configuration changes, disconnect on teardown, and let the callback dispatch intent rather than fetch or render.

items.label: MDN Intersection Observer API
items.description: Review observer roots, thresholds, root margins, and lifecycle behavior.

blocks.title: Avoid a leaky component
blocks.text: If callers must synchronize cursor, loading, observer state, and retries, the component exports its races. Prefer immutable inputs and guarded commands.

PageLoader.load receives the complete query identity, normalized filters, sort order, page limit, opaque cursor, and AbortSignal. Its result contains ordered items, the next opaque cursor, and an optional ordering version. The controller validates the cursor relationship, ignores a stale generation, deduplicates by item identity, and never derives a next cursor from list length.

blocks.title: A query change through the loader

steps.title: Observe intent
steps.text: IntersectionObserver is a prefetch hint; the visible Load More button invokes the same admission path.

steps.title: Admit once
steps.text: Reject repeat requests for a cursor already pending or committed.

steps.title: Merge safely
steps.text: Validate the generation, normalize entities, append unseen IDs, and advance only after a successful page.

steps.title: Restore context
steps.text: After navigation or variable-height measurement, mount the anchor and restore its intra-item offset.
